item.text:
**Configuration.** `httpx.Timeout` defines four limits: `connect`, `read`, `write`, and `pool`. `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONFIG` sets each to 5 seconds. Set `timeout=` on `Client` or `AsyncClient` for a client-wide default, override it per request, or pass `None` to disable it. [`httpx/_config.py:72`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_config.py:72), [`httpx/_config.py:246`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_config.py:246), [`httpx/_client.py:340`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:340)

**Propagation.** `build_request()` writes the effective settings to `request.extensions["timeout"]`. On `send()`, `_set_timeout()` fills in the client default if the extension is missing. An existing timeout extension takes precedence. [`httpx/_client.py:370`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:370), [`httpx/_client.py:584`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:584)

**Enforcement.** The default sync and async transports forward the extension to **httpcore**, which enforces the limits on connection establishment, reads, writes, and waiting for a pooled connection. Each limit applies to its operation, so a request can take longer than five seconds overall. The transports map httpcore’s timeout exceptions to HTTPX exceptions. [`httpx/_transports/default.py:230`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_transports/default.py:230), [`httpx/_transports/default.py:374`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_transports/default.py:374), [`httpx/_transports/default.py:74`](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_transports/default.py:74)
